transcript_header:
Date: 2027-03-02
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jared Miller (Redwood AE); Aisha Khan (Redwood SE); Maya Singh (Prism Health, CTO); Tom Reynolds (Prism Health, Head of Security); Liam O'Connor (Prism Health, Eng Manager)
Recording: Enabled
summary: Discovery focused on Prism Health's security and compliance requirements for deploying LLM inference. Key topics: SOC 2 / ISO scope, SSO/SAML and SCIM for provisioning, RBAC model, audit logs retention, encryption and KMS/BYOK, VPC/private deployment options and dedicated capacity for latency-sensitive workloads. Agreed next steps: send SOC2/ISO docs, schedule SE-led deep dive and benchmark, customer to return security questionnaire.
topics: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 scope
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) tradeoffs
transcript: 00:00 Jared Miller: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, Jared from Redwood here. we got Aisha on the call as well our solutions engineer. um quick roll call?
00:12 Maya Singh: Hi, Maya here, CTO at Prism Health. we got Tom and Liam on as well.
00:20 Tom Reynolds: Tom, head of security. quick note, we got a hard stop at 16:45 pacific.
00:28 Aisha Khan: Awesome, thanks. goal for today is to understand your security posture and what you'd need for hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment, yeah?
00:40 Liam O'Connor: Yep, main drivers are patient data handling, latency for clinical workflows, and vendor compliance (HIPAA-ish).
01:05 Jared Miller: Great. can you walk us through current infra? where do you host data, how do you do SSO, typical retention policies?

01:22 Maya Singh: We run mostly in AWS us-west-2. okta for SSO and SCIM provisioning. retention is currently 7 years for EPHI, but for logs maybe 1 year. we're SOC 2 in progress, ISO discussion pending.

01:45 Tom Reynolds: to be explicit we need SOC 2 Type II evidence for any hosted PII handling, and for anything accessing EPHI we need BAAs and HIPAA controls. encryption keys ideally customer-managed or HSM-backed.

02:10 Aisha Khan: Understood. Redwood supports SOC 2 and we can provide reports for hosted customers; for dedicated/private we do options for customer-managed keys (BYOK) via KMS or HSM integrations. just to clarify, are you leaning hosted first or private?
02:30 Maya Singh: Preference is hosted for speed, but we need strong guarantees. if hosted can't meet KMS BYOK and audit logs retention, we'll consider private.

03:00 Jared Miller: Ok, quick contrasts: hosted gives fastest time-to-value and our managed SOC 2 controls; dedicated is reserved GPU pools with isolation and SLA; private gives you VPC peering or on-prem control, own KMS/HSM, and full audit access. latency vs ops tradeoff.
03:27 Liam O'Connor: For our clinical UI, we need p95 < 300ms on common prompts. cost is a factor, though dedicated looks expensive but predictable.

03:48 Aisha Khan: We can run a benchmark in a dedicated pool to validate p95 and throughput; we also do quantized variants for cost. there's also prefix caching and batching to lower token costs without lengthening latency significantly.

04:20 Tom Reynolds: On the compliance side we need audit logs that show user id, request metadata, model version, and whether the call was served from cache vs fresh. retention configurable to 1y or longer, plus export to your SIEM.

04:40 Jared Miller: Yep, our audit logs include request/response metadata, model ids, timestamps and user ids. we support export to S3 or directly to Splunk/Datadog via forwarders; retention is configurable and we can push to customer-owned buckets for longer retention.
05:05 Maya Singh: And SSO? we use Okta for SAML 2.0 + SCIM for provisioning. we need role mapping to our internal teams.
05:20 Aisha Khan: We support SAML SSO and SCIM; role-based mapping and SCIM group sync. RBAC can be mapped to Okta groups; we also do token-level roles and route-level permissions in the Console.
05:50 Tom Reynolds: What about emergency access, break-glass, and audit trails for admin actions?
06:05 Jared Miller: We support audit of admin actions with immutable logs and alerting. break-glass can be done via temporary role elevation with time-limited tokens and full write-to-audit logging.
06:40 Aisha Khan: On encryption: in-transit is TLS1.2+; at-rest we support AES-256. for KMS we integrate with AWS KMS or customer HSMs for BYOK. HSM-backed keys are possible for Private deploys.
07:05 Tom Reynolds: We need attestations about key access: who at Redwood can access raw keys or plaintext?

07:18 Jared Miller: For hosted with customer-managed KMS, Redwood never sees plaintext keys. Redwood personnel access is restricted, with least-privilege, and access logs. we can provide separation-of-duties docs and personnel access rosters upon NDA.
07:45 Liam O'Connor: Data residency: do you have region support and data at rest in region?

07:58 Aisha Khan: Yes, region pinning is supported for both hosted and dedicated; private can be deployed to your VPC in-region to meet residency requirements. we have a regional model catalog and routing policy.
08:25 Maya Singh: A question on model variants like if you've quantized models, do you have different security profiles? like are logs scrubbed differently?
08:40 Aisha Khan: Logs don't change by quantization; however, model variant names and versions are logged. we also offer a sanitize layer or opt-in PII redaction for transcripts before storage.
09:05 Tom Reynolds: PII redaction is interesting. is that pre-storage or post? we need to see how reversible it is.

09:20 Jared Miller: We can do pre-storage redaction using deterministic redactors; full audit trail of redaction decisions is kept. reversible redaction would require keys and is typically only for bespoke PII workflows under private deployment.
09:45 Liam O'Connor: On incident response how do you notify customers for incidents affecting availability or data exposure?

10:00 Jared Miller: We have tiered incident response SLAs, email+phone for Sev1, and an incident page + post-incident report. for Dedicated customers we include a 24/7 on-call escalation. we also provide root cause and remediation steps.
10:20 Tom Reynolds: Good. can you walk through how audit logs are exported and what retention options are available?

10:35 Aisha Khan: Sure. logs are captured centrally; you can set retention to 30/90/365+ days. exports to customer-owned S3, GCS, or SIEM. for Private, logs stay in your VPC and you control retention entirely.
11:10 Maya Singh: Are there any parts of the call path that touch plaintext data outside of our region for hosted?
11:25 Jared Miller: By default hosted processes in our regional clusters; we can configure region pinning. keys for BYOK remain in your KMS region, Redwood only receives tokens and encrypted blobs.
11:50 Liam O'Connor: Ok on SSO provisioning behow fast is SCIM sync? near real-time?
12:05 Aisha Khan: SCIM is near-real-time; group membership changes are reflected within minutes. you can also trigger manual syncs via the Console.
12:20 Tom Reynolds: On RBAC scoping do you support per-team model pinning? e.g., only allow certain groups to use higher-capacity models or dedicated routes?
12:38 Jared Miller: Yes, route- and model-level RBAC is supported; you can configure policies so only certain Okta groups can call specific models or endpoints, and we can enforce quotas per team.
13:02 Maya Singh: About log granularity we need request/response hashes, not raw responses stored for long because of patient data. is hashing supported?

13:18 Aisha Khan: Absolutely. we support storing hashes of responses and request payloads; full payload storage can be disabled or encrypted to customer buckets. we also offer token-sampling for diagnostics with explicit consent.
13:45 Tom Reynolds: Regarding SOC 2, what's in your scope today and can you share the last Type II report?

14:00 Jared Miller: We can share our SOC 2 Type II report and ISO27001 summary. for hosted we have full coverage for the inference product; dedicated/private have similar controls but the attestation scope differs we'll clarify in the doc.
14:22 Maya Singh: Timeline wise we want to pilot in April if docs look good. security sign-off is blocker.

14:35 Jared Miller: Sounds good next steps we'll send SOC2, ISO scope, architecture VPC peering guide, and a proposed pilot plan for Dedicated capacity. we'll also schedule an SE-led technical deep dive and run benchmarks for p95 latency.
15:00 Liam O'Connor: For the benchmark, can you simulate our typical prompt distribution? we have a set of 200 typical prompts, many short but some long context windows.
15:18 Aisha Khan: Yes, please send the prompt set ideally as anonymized inputs; we'll run it against a dedicated pool and provide token-cost estimates and latency percentiles.
15:40 Tom Reynolds: A couple of quick nitty-gritty: do you support immutable audit storage and WORM for compliance?
15:53 Jared Miller: We support write-once buckets for audit logs via S3 Object Lock for hosted exports, and private deployments can use your own retention/WORM policies.
16:05 Maya Singh: Ok we're at our stop time. last check are there any blockers for you to share the SOC2 right away?
16:15 Jared Miller: No blockers; I'll drop it in the shared drive and via the secure link. Aisha will follow up on benchmark logistics. we'll add the docs to the CRM ticket.
16:25 Maya Singh: thanks everyone. appreciate it.
16:30 Jared Miller: Thanks all recap in an email with attachments and action items. talk soon. bye.
